ours.name: "ours" held-out set
ours.about: the project's held-out clips (eval/clipset/heldout_2026-11-23b.manifest.json), "audited once, never tuned on": 84 of the 97 clips were read once by the 0.6.0 results audit and 13 are unseen (sealed log entries 1b-3); the set was also read for quality by release measurements on 2026-11-23 to 11-26 while our encoder changed, and no lever is recorded as chosen from it

vc1k.name: VC-1K
vc1k.about: phone video calls from Meta's VC-1K dataset (CC BY-NC 4.0); numbers only; the headline leaves out the 9 clips our encoders were tuned on

aomctc.name: AOM-CTC
aomctc.about: the AOM common test conditions' sequences (eval/clipset/aomctc_bp3.manifest.json), A2 included; its 12 low-delay clips (A3-A5) are in-sample for ours

fast.name: Fast subset (30 clips)
fast.about: 30 of the 97 clips of the "ours" held-out set (eval/clipset/fast-subset.json), chosen once from the BP-4 per-clip results so that it tracks the full set, and never tuned on. On both AWS machines every one of the 64 current families' BD-J on the 30 is within 1 point of the median offset from its full-set BD-J (check V17: median offset +0.36 on x86 and +0.48 on Arm, largest deviation 0.69 and 0.73), with the same front; so figures on it read about half a point above the full set's. It is the set the slower machines (Apple M4, Jetson Orin Nano) time
